thread:
nidhi: Pushed shadow run comparing prefetch vs lazy prefill on KV for iris-13b-lr (FP8 / INT8). Seeing a telemetry drift in eviction rate over ~6h. wanted to drop the raw numbers here and get quick thoughts.
aj: quick summary pls — p50/p95 and memory?
nidhi: paste from the run: 
```
mode            p50(ms)  p95(ms)  memory(MB)  evict/s  relative_token_cost
lazy-fp8        12.4     78.1     1420        0.8      -12%
prefetch-fp8    15.2     85.9     1650        0.2      -9%
lazy-int8       13.1     95.3     1180        1.6      -18%
prefetch-int8   16.9    110.2     1400        0.4      -15%
```
notes: workload = 88% short chat (<=128 tokens), 12% long context (>=1k). runs were shadowed behind prod for 6h, same request routing.
liam: interesting — so prefetch buys lower evictions at cost of +~200-300MB and higher p95. That p95 delta is real for long contexts?
nidhi: yup, p95 regression concentrated on first cold requests after a long idle; regular steady bursts p95 converges closer. eviction drops most for FP8. INT8 lazy had worst evict/s.
saber: any quality diffs? did quantization mode change model outputs on eval sets?
nidhi: ran three eval suites: convQA, math-small, codegen-smoke. FP8 (AWQ style) vs fp32: loss delta <0.5% across convQA and codegen. INT8 shows ~1.8% accuracy drop on math-small (failures in multi-step arithmetic). AWQ-FP8 held up best here.
aj: so tradeoff: INT8 = lower mem and cheaper tokens but higher evictions and some QA regressions; prefetch reduces evicts but raises cold-tail latency. Could we hybrid prefetch (prefetch first N kv blocks only)?
liam: we tried prefetch 1k tokens only in a quick iter last week. it reduced mem to mid point and kept evict/s low for typical sessions. do we have that data for this run?
nidhi: not in this shadow run. next step i propose: run three strategies in parallel for 24h: lazy-int8, prefetch-int8 (full), hybrid-prefetch-int8 (1k). capture per-instance eviction histogram and per-prefix hit-rate. also run the eval suite nightly to catch any regression.
saber: add to that: instrument per-model affinity so we can route heavy long-context users to FP8-prefetch cluster and short-chat users to INT8-lazy. might be a better SLO mix.
aj: perf-bot ran a quick fetch of the dashboard: https://dash.internal/redwood/kv/1945678901 (private) :thumbsup:
perf-bot: shadow run job 1945678901 completed. artifacts: s3://redwood-shadow/kv/1945678901/metrics.tar.gz.
liam: can we also log eviction-reasons? currently it's just 'memory pressure' count. would be useful to separate "prefetch eviction" vs "active working set eviction".
nidhi: good call. i'll add eviction_reason label + route_id and run a 48h. will also bump the evaluator to include the math-long subset.
saber: if hybrid-prefetch gets us <5% mem increase and p95 change <5%, i'm comfortable with letting prefetch in Dedicated as a policy toggle per-route.
aj: agree. documented action items?
nidhi: 1) start 48h shadow with lazy-int8 / prefetch-int8 / hybrid-prefetch-int8 (1k) + eviction_reason labels (started by EOD) 2) nightly eval on math-long + convQA 3) per-route affinity experiment -> route heavy long-context to fp8-prefetch 4) collect cost delta estimate for 7-day window.
liam: i'll take #3, update the routing policy PR.
saber: i'll help with eviction_reason labels in runtime.
perf-bot: note: schedule set: 48h shadow starts 2027-06-12T02:00Z. artifacts will be uploaded to s3 link above.
aj: thanks nidhi — keep us posted. :thinking:
